about: Guy Hammering Nails Into Sand is a photo of a gray-haired man crouched at the very edge of the water on a beach, hammer raised, carefully tapping nails into the wet sand. A neat line of nails already sticks up along the waterline where the waves wash over them. It is the picture of determined effort that cannot possibly hold, since the next wave will undo it. Labeled, it turns into a commentary on futility: one thing tries to pin down another, while something vast and indifferent sloshes over all of it.
usage:
There are three labels. The first sits on the man and names who or what is doing the work. The second sits on the row of nails and names the tool or method being used. The third sits over the sea and names the huge, shapeless thing that the effort is trying to fix in place.

The format is at its best when it is a little philosophical: humanity, language and the universe; a developer, documentation and the codebase; a student, flashcards and the entire syllabus. The sea label should be the biggest idea, since it is the one swallowing everything else.
ideas: the indescribable nature of the universe
